def maximize_elements(tuples1, tuples2):
    """
    Given two lists of tuples, return a new list where for each position i (0..n-1),
    result[i] is formed by taking the maximum element-wise from all input tuples.
    
    Example:
        maximize_elements(((1, 3), (4, 5), (2, 9), (1, 10)), 
                          ((6, 7), (3, 9), (1, 1), (7, 3)))
        == ((6, 7), (4, 9), (2, 9), (7, 10))
    """
    # Ensure both lists have the same number of tuples; if not, handle as needed.
    n = min(len(tuples1), len(tuples2))

    result = []
    for i in range(n):
        t1 = tuples1[i]
        t2 = tuples2[i]
        
        # Compute element-wise max up to the shorter tuple length at this position
        m_len = min(len(t1), len(t2))
        row_max = [max(a, b) for a, b in zip(t1[:m_len], t2[:m_len])]

        # If one tuple is longer than the other, extend with its extra elements.
        if len(t1) > m_len:
            row_max.extend(t1[m_len:])
        elif len(t2) > m_len:
            row_max.extend(t2[m_len:])

        result.append(tuple(row_max))

    return tuple(result)


# Test the example from the prompt
if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert maximize_elements(((1, 3), (4, 5), (2, 9), (1, 10)), 
                             ((6, 7), (3, 9), (1, 1), (7, 3))) == \
           ((6, 7), (4, 9), (2, 9), (7, 10))
    print("Assertion passed.")
